mainTopic: How long a husband's הפרה lasts for vows of עינוי נפש compared with vows that affect the couple, and what the משנה's vow 'אם ארחץ' actually said.
overview: The משנה ends with רבי יוסי's narrower definition of נדרי עינוי נפש: a vow counts only if she truly cannot get the item anywhere else. The גמרא asks why a husband could cancel only vows of עינוי נפש, since a ברייתא says he can also cancel vows that affect their relationship (דברים שבינו לבינה). A first answer says he can cancel both, but a relationship vow comes back after a divorce. That answer is attacked from רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who advises cancelling such a vow in case of a future divorce, which shows the cancellation still holds afterward. So the גמרא gives a new answer: every הפרה lasts forever for the husband himself. Only a vow of עינוי נפש stays cancelled even if she marries someone else. The גמרא then asks what the משנה's vow 'אם ארחץ' (if I bathe) actually said. It tests the reading 'all produce of the world is forbidden to me if I bathe' and rejects it twice. For the תנא קמא she could simply avoid bathing, and for רבי יוסי the vow would clearly count as affliction.

steps.title: רבי יוסי defines true vows of affliction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the earlier examples are not נדרי עינוי נפש. A vow counts only if it really leaves her without the item: produce of the whole world, or a single storekeeper when he is the only source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: These are not vows of affliction. These are vows of affliction: if she said, "The produce of the whole world is קונם for me," he can cancel it. If she said, "The produce of this country is forbidden to me," he can bring her produce from another country. If she said, "The produce of this storekeeper is forbidden to me," he cannot cancel it. But if he could only get his food from that storekeeper, he may cancel it. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with רבי יוסי disagreeing about which vows count as real affliction. For him, a vow is affliction only if she truly cannot get the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key test for רבי יוסי is whether there is another way to get the item. Banning one country's produce or one store's produce is not real suffering, because the husband can buy elsewhere. The one exception is when that store is the family's only source of food.

steps.title: Can a husband cancel only vows of affliction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה means a husband can cancel only vows of עינוי נפש. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that he can also cancel vows that affect the couple's relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only vows of affliction that he can cancel, while vows without affliction he cannot cancel? But a ברייתא teaches: "Between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter" teaches that a husband can cancel vows that affect matters between him and her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's impression that only vows of affliction can be cancelled. It brings a ברייתא that adds a second kind of vow the husband can cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to limit הפרה to vows of עינוי נפש. The ברייתא reads the פסוק "בין איש לאשתו" as including vows that harm the marriage, even with no suffering. That looks like a contradiction.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that vows affecting the relationship can also be cancelled, so the משנה cannot mean only affliction vows.

steps.title: Both kinds can be cancelled, but they last differently
steps.stepSummary: A husband can cancel both kinds of vows. Cancelling a vow of עינוי נפש lasts forever. Cancelling a vow that only affects the couple works only during the marriage, and the vow returns after a divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: He can cancel both these and those. But vows of affliction he cancels forever. Vows without affliction are cancelled while she is under him, and once he divorces her, her vow takes effect on her. This applies to matters between him and her that have no affliction. But if they involve affliction, her vow does not take effect on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the husband can cancel both kinds of vows. The difference is how long the cancellation lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list is not about which vows can be cancelled. It is about which cancellations are permanent. Affliction vows stay cancelled even after a divorce, while relationship-only vows come back once the marriage ends.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי suggests the cancellation lasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that a relationship vow returns after a divorce. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the husband should cancel such a vow in case he divorces her, which implies his cancellation keeps working after the divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And vows without affliction, when he divorces her, do they really take effect on her? But we learned: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says, he should cancel it, in case he divorces her and she becomes forbidden to him. This shows that if he divorces her after he cancelled the vow from the start, the cancellation still holds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It quotes a משנה from later in the מסכת that seems to say a cancellation done during the marriage stays in force after the divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי tells the husband to cancel the vow now so it won't cause trouble after a divorce. That advice only makes sense if the cancellation still works after the divorce. This contradicts the previous step, which said relationship vows come back.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן בן נורי advises cancelling in case of a future divorce, which implies the cancellation keeps working after the divorce even for a vow with no affliction.

steps.title: Every cancellation is permanent for the husband; the difference is about others
steps.stepSummary: Both kinds of vows are permanently cancelled for the husband himself. Only vows of עינוי נפש are also cancelled 'for others', meaning if she later marries another man. The משנה's opening line is read to mean exactly this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: for both kinds of vows, the husband's cancellation really works. The difference is this. A vow of affliction he cancels both for himself and for others. A vow with no affliction he cancels for himself, but not for others. So the משנה means: 'These are the vows he cancels both for himself and for others: vows that involve affliction.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן בן נורי by changing how we understand the two kinds of vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said a relationship vow comes back after a divorce, and Step 4 showed that cannot be right. Now the rule is that every הפרה lasts forever as far as this husband is concerned, even if he divorces her and later remarries her. A vow with no עינוי נפש is cancelled only 'for himself' (לעצמו), so it takes effect if she marries a different man, while a vow of עינוי נפש stays cancelled even then.

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The husband should cancel a relationship vow now, because the cancellation protects him even if he divorces her and later remarries her.

steps.title: What exact vow does the משנה mean by 'if I bathe'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה's case of 'אם ארחץ' was actually worded, setting up the next steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's case of 'if I bathe': what exactly is she saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and is setting up the next move. It asks what the woman actually said when she made the vow 'אם ארחץ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'If I bathe' is only a condition. It does not say what she forbade on herself. So the גמרא needs to know the full wording of the vow before it can judge whether it is עינוי נפש.

steps.title: If the vow depends on bathing, she can simply avoid bathing
steps.stepSummary: Suppose she said, 'All produce of the world is forbidden to me if I bathe.' Then she does not need a הפרה at all: she can just not bathe.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she said, 'Produce of the world is קונם for me if I bathe,' why does she need a cancellation? Let her not bathe, and this produce of the world will not be forbidden to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation of the case and immediately shows a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the food becomes forbidden only if she bathes. She has an easy way to avoid suffering: don't bathe. So why would the תנא קמא call this a vow of affliction that needs a הפרה?

steps.title: A second problem: רבי יוסי would surely call such a vow affliction
steps.stepSummary: If the vow put all produce of the world at stake, רבי יוסי himself would agree it is עינוי נפש. If she bathes, she is left with no food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: in such a case, would רבי יוסי say these are not vows of affliction? Perhaps she will bathe, and the produce of the world will be forbidden to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, separate attack on the same suggestion, this time from רבי יוסי's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 1, רבי יוסי said that losing produce of the whole world is real עינוי נפש. If she ever bathes, that is exactly what happens here. So his calling the 'if I bathe' case 'not affliction' does not fit this version of the vow either.
